accuracy.evidence: Every algebra line was checked by expansion: (x + 3)² ≡ x² + 6x + 9, x(x − 2) + 1 ≡ (x − 1)², (a + b)² − (a − b)² ≡ 4ab, (x + 2)(x − 2) + 4 ≡ x², and (2n + 1)(2n + 3) ≡ 4(n² + 2n + 1) − 1. Counterexamples are exact (x = 1 gives 16 and 10; 2 and 4). Curriculum wording matches CCSS A-APR.4 and the DfE GCSE programme of study proof statement.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented proof errors: examples treated as proof (Test the claim prediction, number-fact prediction, p3, challenge), disproof thought to need every x (m2, 'all' feedback), working on both sides (Build prediction, m3), (a + b)² as a² + b² (slip options, m-challenge), sign error over a bracket (proof 2 slip, m6), one letter for two different odd numbers (form card, fact 3 slip) and stopping before the revealing form (fact 2, m5).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagproof is the only lab that tests a claim by dragging x along a number line with live left and right values and coloured agree or differ marks, then builds proofs one valid line at a time from LHS to RHS. Max 6-token overlap with any existing lab is under 4 percent (flag_altsp, flag_mixed, flag_whyrule), and no other lab uses the identity symbol or proof chains.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each step is one idea of the A-APR.4 proof sequence: ≡ versus =, testing versus proving (a value that agrees at x = 0 then fails at x = 1), the layout of a proof as a chain from one side to the other, general forms 2n, 2n + 1, n and n + 1, and finishing by factorising so the fact shows. Wrong choices give the precise algebraic reason, so learners fix the slip, not just retry.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions are asked before acting and each one is then tested in the step: whether agreeing at x = 0 makes an identity, whether to work on both sides, which pair is two consecutive odd numbers (n + 1 and n + 3 is the tempting wrong pick), and whether three examples are a proof. Each reveal explains the reasoning after the learner has committed to an answer.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions rotate answer order and each wrong option has its own explanation: eqn, approx, examples, false, oneex, combine (n² + n is not 2n²), fresh ((a + b)² middle term), zero (a = b = 1 gives 4 and 2), all (they agree at x = 0), big, same and twice. Correct answers build a streak and Another loads the next question.

readability.evidence: Learner text uses short sentences and worked lines with concrete numbers, measured within the learner limit, and the adult text stays under its readability limit while still naming the standards. Symbols are spaced (x + 3)² so they read clearly, and the lab uses a maths serif for expressions and system sans for instructions, with no wall of prose on the canvas.

no_filler.evidence: Every paragraph carries a definition, a worked example or a named mistake: ≡ versus =, the x = 0 trap and x = 1 counterexample, a complete proof of (n + 1)² − n² ≡ 2n + 1, and the consecutive odd product proof. The family tip gives a concrete claim to test and then prove with n, n + 1 and n + 2. No praise padding or vague motivational lines appear anywhere.

mobile.evidence: Checked on a 360 px Android and iPhone 13 walkthrough in both themes: the x knob is a 32 px target on a full-width line, decision pads and option cards are full-width and at least 50 px tall, wrapped text never overlaps, and every canvas action has a matching button below (x − 1, x + 1, Identity, Not an identity, and each option) for users who cannot drag.

accessibility.evidence: axe reports no violations in light or dark theme on desktop and phone. The canvas aria-label and a live region announce x, both side values and whether they agree, every proof line and each feedback message. All actions are buttons with aria-labels, colours come from theme tokens and pass contrast, and reduced motion skips the feedback delays.
